explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration with this content. The theorem says that every element of `posDetInt n` lies in the commensurator of `SLnZ n` inside `GL_n(ℚ)`. Both are the library's own definitions: `posDetInt n` is the matrices with integer entries and positive determinant, and `SLnZ n` is the image of `SL_n(ℤ)`. The proof just applies the library's own lemma `mem_commensurator_of_hasIntEntries`. The word `commensurator` appears in only two Mathlib files. `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Commensurable.lean` has only general facts: `refl`, `trans`, `inf_left`, `map`, `commensurator_mem_iff`, `eq`, and similar. `Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean` sets up the abstract `IsHeckeTriple` structure. Neither says anything about `SL_n(ℤ)`, `GL_n(ℚ)` or integer matrices.
